title: Global grain market
summary:
Main
By Michalis Voutsinas
For most of the past three years, the global grain market has been defined by abundance. Successive record harvests across the Americas, a remarkable recovery in Black Sea exports despite the ongoing war, and the gradual unwinding of the 2022 commodity price shock combined to push food prices down by roughly a fifth between 2022 and 2025. That period of relative comfort is now being challenged on two fronts.
